newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK PRESIDENT RETURNS BANK SELLOFF LAW TO PARLT.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK PRESIDENT RETURNS BANK SELLOFF LAW TO PARLT.

text.p: Slovak President Michal Kovac on Wednesday returned a law barring bank privatisation to parliament, the president's office said in a statement.

"President Michal Kovac on Wednesday acknowledged the government's request not to sign the law barring privatisation of banks and returned it to parliament for re-assessment," the presidential statement said.

On February 13, parliament approved a measure adding the four state-controlled financial institutions to a list of strategic companies, effectively halting the bank selloff till the end of the year 2003 at the earliest.

Through the NPF, the state controls 91.3 percent of the largest savings bank Slovenska Sporitelna , 50.5 percent if insurer Slovenska Poistovna , some 35 percent in bank IRB and about 51.49 percent in the largest commercial bank VUB.

"The postponement of bank privatisation may slow down Slovakia's integration into the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD), and can endanger further economic reforms" the government said in requesting Kovac return the law.
The government also said that one of the factors for proceeding in restructuring the banking sector was an increase of bank capital resources.
The NPF expected to increase the banks' capital resources through the sale of shares from its portfolio.
"The NPF also wanted to use the fiscal potential of buyers to speed up the process of bank restructuring as one of the main privatisation criteria," the government said.

Opposition parties and minor coalition partner, the ultra-left Workers Party (ZRS), which defected from the coalition in the first vote on the law barring bank privatisation, said it would again vote for the postponement of the selloff.
